Nikita Shivhare vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8
November, 2024
Neutral Citation No. 2024:Mphc-Gwl:19385
 1 Cra-11244
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Gwalior

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajendra Kumar Vani

On The 8 th Of November, 2024
 Criminal Appeal No. 11244 of 2024
 Nikita Shivhare
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Ajay Kumar Dwivedi - Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri Saket Udeniya - Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1/State.
 Shri Jyotirmay Sharma - Advocate for respondent No.2.
 Order

1. This criminal appeal (first) under Section 14-(2) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been filed against the order dated 18.09.2024 passed by Special Judge (Atrocities) Gwalior, in Bail Application No.2473/2024 whereby the application moved by the appellant for grant of anticipatory bail under Section 482 of BNSS as she is apprehending her arrest in connection with Crime No.81/2023 registered at Police Station Gwalior District Gwalior for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 346, 363, 506, 120-B of IPC and Sections 3(2)(v), 3(2)(va) and 3(1)(w)(ii) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, has been rejected.

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.

Though in the statement under NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-GWL:19385 2 CRA-11244-2024 Section 164 of Cr.P.C. of the prosecutrix, name of present appellant has been revealed that she along with other co-accused persons and prosecutrix travelled to Mumbai, but no overt act of present appellant is shown.
As per the statement of the prosecutrix, she simply travelled upto Mumbai along with prosecutrix.

Co-accused Shailendra Sharma, Smt. Sharda and Smt. Rekha Shivhare have been granted anticipatory bail vide orders dated 07.08.2023, 29.03.2023 and 02.03.2023 passed in Criminal Appeal Nos.4260/2023,
4178/2023 and 3115/2023.

Though anticipatory bail application of co-accsued Dimpal has been dismissed vide order dated 29.08.2024 passed in Criminal Appeal No.9373/2024, but the act of Dimpal is quite different from the present appellant as revealed from the statement of the prosecutrix under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
She is ready and willing to abide by all the terms and conditions which may be imposed by this Court.

On these grounds, learned counsel prays for grant Nikita Shivhare vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107048015/
1 of anticipatory bail to the appellant.
3.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the State as well as complainant opposed the bail application by submitting that act of present applicant is revealed in the statement of the prosecutrix.
Though they fairly conceded that except travelling upto Mumbai, no overt act of present appellant is revealed from the documents.

4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
5.

Considering the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and attending facts and circumstances of the case, but without NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19385 3 CRA-11244-2024 expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this appeal is allowed by setting aside the order dated 18.09.2024 passed by Special Judge (Atrocities), Gwalior in Bail Application No.2473/2024 and it is directed that in case if the appellant appears before the Investigating Officer/trial Court within fifteen days from today and furnishes personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lac) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned Investigating Officer/trial Court, then she shall be released on anticipatory bail.
